question: Tell me about a time you chose to make a Slack channel or a data system open rather than private. How did you balance transparency with the right level of access?

raiseTranscript.text: On my team we had a private channel for our sprint metrics. I suggested making it public after a teammate from another squad asked for visibility into our velocity trends.
What happened after you opened it?
Two other teams started using the same format and shared their own numbers. I added a note that anyone could join but we kept the write access to our squad leads.
How did you decide on the access rules?
My manager reviewed the membership list first and we limited posting rights to avoid noise.

junior.raiseFeedback: Raises the bar for junior. Principle tested is Break down silos. Candidate described moving a private sprint metrics channel to public after another squad requested velocity data. Quote: "I added a note that anyone could join but we kept the write access to our squad leads." Manager review step shows coachability and ownership of own work. Two teams adopted the format shows local but measurable cross-team visibility. Biggest strength is clear, low-scope decision with explicit access guardrails.

raiseTranscript.text: Our payment service metrics lived in a private Looker folder. I moved the key dashboards to a shared space after two partner teams asked for the same numbers during quarterly planning.
I created a viewer group that included the partner teams and kept editor rights to our service owners. I also posted the change in the platform channel with a one-pager on how to read the data.
The partner teams reduced duplicate queries by 40 percent and one of them contributed a new filter we adopted.

raiseTranscript.text: Our customer data warehouse had many private datasets that slowed partner teams. I sponsored a default-shared policy with exception-based private folders and required every new dataset to justify privacy in the data council.
How did you manage the change?

I worked with legal and security to define the exception criteria and had each org assign a data steward. We tracked adoption weekly and after six months private datasets dropped from 65 percent to 22 percent.
Some teams worried about exposing unreviewed models so we added a staging area and review SLA that kept velocity steady.
